🇺🇸🇮🇷 Trump already fought this exact war against China... He lost. Ian Bremmer says forget Iraq or Vietnam, the real precedent is the tariff war. Trump hit Beijing expecting capitulation, China shut down the critical minerals supply chain, American factories faced going dark, and Trump backed down into engagement: "When he hits them hard, they hit back. The difference here is that Trump does not yet believe or accept that the Iranians really have far more leverage over the outcome than he is prepared to understand and accept." Two sides who agree on their relative strength negotiate. Two sides who don't keep fighting, and that disagreement is the war now. @ianbremmer Video Mario Nawfal (@MarioNawfal) 🇺🇸🇮🇷 Trump remains trapped because he still refuses to accept how much leverage Iran possesses. He still thinks overwhelming American power will eventually force Tehran to give in, and political scientist Ian Bremmer says that's the mistake keeping this war alive. Instead, Iran has shown it can keep raising the economic cost of the war without crossing Trump's red lines. Ian doesn't think Iran believes it can defeat the U.S militarily; it believes it can make continuing the war more painful than ending it. And so far, it's working. Trump keeps threatening to destroy Iran's infrastructure, eliminate its leadership and dramatically escalate the conflict. But Ian points to something more revealing than Trump's rhetoric: His actions. Despite months of fighting, Trump has avoided the biggest escalations. No ground invasion, no sustained campaign against Iran's energy sector, and no full-scale assault on the country's leadership. Even after American casualties, his instinct has repeatedly been to play them down rather than use them to justify a much wider war. And Tehran has noticed. It increasingly sees a president who talks like he's preparing for total war but behaves like someone searching for an exit. The bigger problem, Ian says, is inside the White House itself. Trump's advisers know the military and economic costs are mounting, and many want the war to end, but very few are willing to tell Trump the uncomfortable truth: Iran has far more leverage over how this ends than Washington expected. Until Trump accepts that reality, Ian believes a genuine compromise remains unlikely. @ianbremmer Video — http://nitter.perennialte.ch/MarioNawfal/status/2080728471190548732#m

Dans ces heures où les flammes éprouvent durement notre pays, la France révèle ce qu’elle est : un peuple uni, qui se serre les coudes. Merci à nos sapeurs-pompiers, à nos militaires, aux forces de sécurité civile, à nos gendarmes et policiers, ainsi qu’aux agriculteurs et entrepreneurs, qui par leur engagement et leur courage, combattent sans relâche les incendies. Tous les moyens civils et militaires sont mobilisés : moyens aériens de la Sécurité civile, Canadair, Dash, hélicoptères bombardiers d’eau, renforts venus de toute la France. Une première illustre la capacité d’adaptation de nos armées : l’A400M est engagé en appui des opérations. Aux côtés des habitants, de toutes les familles touchées, des déplacés à qui on pense, la Nation est pleinement engagée. Les maires, les élus locaux et les services de l’État, préfets et agents des Préfectures, sont en première ligne pour protéger, accompagner et préparer l’après. Ils peuvent compter sur le soutien indéfectible de la République. Merci à la Roumanie, la Croatie, l’Allemagne, au Portugal, à la Suède, la Suisse, la République tchèque et la Slovaquie pour leur précieux soutien. C’est l’Europe. Dans l’épreuve, elle fait vivre la solidarité qui la fonde. Nos pensées vont aussi à l’Espagne, à l’Italie, à la Grèce et à tous les peuples qui affrontent eux aussi les incendies. Dans le Sud-Ouest, en particulier en Gironde et dans les Landes ; dans le Sud, notamment dans le Var, les Hautes-Alpes et la Haute-Corse ; en Occitanie, en particulier dans les Pyrénées-Orientales, mais aussi partout où les flammes frappent, des milliers d’hectares ont été ravagés, des habitations détruites, des activités interrompues, des vies bouleversées. Nous reconstruirons, nous réparerons et nous serons présents aussi longtemps qu’il le faudra.

The Meeting noted the progress in the ASEAN Plus Three (APT) cooperation over the past year and discussed its future direction. The Meeting reaffirmed the commitment to further strengthening and deepening the APT process, which remains a main vehicle for advancing regional community-building and in promoting peace, stability, security, and prosperity in the East Asian region with ASEAN as the driving force. The Meeting also recognised the importance of APT cooperation in supporting the realisation of ASEAN 2045: Our Shared Future and its strategic plans, the Initiative for ASEAN Integration (IAI) Work Plan IV (2021–2025), including their contributions to the development and implementation of the IAI Work Plan V (2026–2030), as well as deeper regional integration in East Asia. The difference here is that Trump does not yet believe or accept that the Iranians really have far more leverage over the outcome than he is prepared to understand and accept." Two sides who agree on their relative strength negotiate. Two sides who don't keep fighting, and that disagreement is the war now. @ianbremmer Video Mario Nawfal (@MarioNawfal) 🇺🇸🇮🇷 Trump remains trapped because he still refuses to accept how much leverage Iran possesses. He still thinks overwhelming American power will eventually force Tehran to give in, and political scientist Ian Bremmer says that's the mistake keeping this war alive. Instead, Iran has shown it can keep raising the economic cost of the war without crossing Trump's red lines. Ian doesn't think Iran believes it can defeat the U.S militarily; it believes it can make continuing the war more painful than ending it. And so far, it's working. Trump keeps threatening to destroy Iran's infrastructure, eliminate its leadership and dramatically escalate the conflict. But Ian points to something more revealing than Trump's rhetoric: His actions. Despite months of fighting, Trump has avoided the biggest escalations. No ground invasion, no sustained campaign against Iran's energy sector, and no full-scale assault on the country's leadership. Even after American casualties, his instinct has repeatedly been to play them down rather than use them to justify a much wider war. And Tehran has noticed. It increasingly sees a president who talks like he's preparing for total war but behaves like someone searching for an exit. The bigger problem, Ian says, is inside the White House itself. Trump's advisers know the military and economic costs are mounting, and many want the war to end, but very few are willing to tell Trump the uncomfortable truth: Iran has far more leverage over how this ends than Washington expected. Тривожно 🫂 First Corps Azov of the National Guard of Ukraine (@azov_media) The advance of two armies and a tank division of the Russian armed forces was repelled: forces of the First Corps Azov of the National Guard of Ukraine destroyed dozens of units of equipment and a large number of occupier personnel. On July 22, the occupiers, using forces of the 8th and 41st Armies along with the 90th Tank Division, attempted an assault in the sector held by the First Corps Azov of the National Guard of Ukraine, involving dozens of units of armored and light vehicles. The 41st Guards Combined Arms Army and the 90th Guards Vitebsk-Novgorod Tank Division of the Russian armed forces advanced from the area of the settlement of Novoekonomichne, while forces of the 8th Guards Combined Arms Army simultaneously advanced from the area of the village of Vozdvyzhenka. For four hours, they attempted to enter settlements in the area of the village of Shakhove. The enemy attempted to deny the sky to Ukrainian forces using "Gerbera" and "Lancet" strike drones. A modern Russian "Tornado-S" MLRS, which was being used to support the assault, was also destroyed. Forces of the First Corps Azov of the National Guard of Ukraine, together with attached units, blocked the path of the advancing mechanized columns. Mine-explosive obstacles were laid on the approaches to the positions of the Ukrainian Defense Forces, and bridges were damaged by tactical aviation. During the assault, the Russians attempted to restore the crossings using pontoons, but these were destroyed by tactical aviation of the Air Force of the Armed Forces of Ukraine (AFU). As a result of the professional actions of all units involved under the command of the First Corps Azov of the National Guard of Ukraine, using barrel artillery, multiple launch rocket systems, and attack drones, the following were destroyed: 7 tanks, 6 armored combat vehicles, 1 BM-21 "Grad" MLRS, 1 "Tornado-S" MLRS, 3 units of special equipment, and 47 units of light vehicles. 123 occupiers were eliminated, and 29 were wounded. The mechanized assault was repelled. We thank the units of the First Corps Azov of the National Guard of Ukraine, the SBU's "A" Special Operations Center, the Unmanned Systems Forces, the Air Force of the AFU, units of the State Border Guard Service of Ukraine, in particular the Main Department of Unmanned Aerial Systems "Fenix," units of the National Guard of Ukraine, and units of the Armed Forces of Ukraine for their professional and courageous actions. Always ready to repel the enemy's assault through joint efforts! Video — http://nitter.perennialte.ch/azov_media/status/2080974057856491559#m

For many survivors, a health worker may be the first, and sometimes the only, person they turn to. Yet not all health workers are equipped to recognise the signs or provide the necessary support. When almost 1 in 3 women and girls aged 15 and older in our Region experience physical or sexual violence in their lifetime, the health sector cannot afford to be unprepared. This is why I launched a special initiative to strengthen the health sector’s response to violence against women and girls. Training health workers is an essential part of this effort, but it must go hand in hand with the right policies and clear clinical guidance. Scotland has just done something quietly brilliant for its birds 🐦 New buildings across the country will now have to include "swift bricks", hollow bricks built straight into the walls that give birds a safe place to nest. It sounds like a small thing but it isn't. Swift numbers in the UK have fallen by around 60% since the mid-1990s, and one of the biggest reasons is heartbreakingly simple: modern buildings have nowhere for them to go. Swifts have always nested in the nooks and gaps of our houses, and as those disappeared, so did they. The birds themselves make it worse by being loyal to a fault. Swifts return to the exact same nest site year after year, having flown thousands of miles from Africa to get there. When they arrive to find it sealed up, some will keep flying at the spot again and again, sometimes injuring themselves in the process. The bricks cost about £30 each. They need no maintenance, they don't affect insulation, and once they're in the wall, you'd never know they were there. Sparrows, starlings and house martins use them too, all species in trouble for the same reason. One RSPB conservationist put it starkly. In his part of Glasgow, not a single swift bred in 2025, the first time in his 30 years there. He called it "nothing short of heartbreaking." Scotland is the first country in the UK to write this into law. Campaigners are now hoping the rest follows.

MIT filmed a calculus course in black and white decades ago and it still teaches better than most of what shipped this year. Almost nobody watches it. This is Calculus Revisited, Unit 1, Lecture 1, taught by Herb Gross. Analytic geometry from the ground up, chalk on a board, 1 camera locked in place. Gross built the course for adults returning to math after years away. No prerequisites assumed. Every idea earned in front of you instead of quoted from a textbook. The opening move is simple division written on the board. From there he shows why coordinates work at all, the thing most courses skip and every student silently fakes. Watch how slowly he goes. Each step spoken out loud, nothing left implicit, the pace of someone who expects you to actually follow. A backend engineer I know rewatched Unit 1 twice before touching linear algebra and said it fixed a gap he'd carried for 12 years. MIT put the whole course online free under Creative Commons. BOOM! OPEN SOURCE MRI! You can now 3D-print the core of an MRI scanner. A machine that hospitals pay $1.1 million to $3.4 million for has been broken open. The OSI² ONE and its educational siblings deliver real images of heads and limbs for a fraction of the cost, using a permanent-magnet Halbach array, 3D-printed structures, and fully open designs. This is not a toy or a simulation. Working systems already produce in-vivo images in Leiden, Utrecht, Berlin, and Uganda. The magnet alone—396 carefully oriented neodymium cubes in a cylindrical Halbach array—costs about $1,370. A complete scanner lands between $28,500 and $68,000 depending on the console and coils you choose. No superconducting magnets. No liquid helium. No specialized power infrastructure. It runs from a standard wall outlet and weighs roughly 150 kg. The physics is elegant. A Halbach array arranges permanent magnets so their fields reinforce inside the bore and nearly cancel outside. The result is a usable 50 mT field strong enough for diagnostic-quality imaging of extremities and the head when paired with clever gradient coils, RF coils, and modern reconstruction. Spatial resolution reaches about 1.5 × 1.5 × 5 mm³. The designs are modular: build the magnet first, verify and shim the field with a 3D-printer-turned-field-scanner, then add gradients and RF hardware. The plans are public Everything needed to replicate or improve the system lives in open repositories: • Primary project hub and documentation: opensourceimaging.org/projec… • Full OSI² repositories (hardware, software, magnets): gitlab.com/osii/ • Educational build focused on the Halbach frame, shimming, gradients, and student workshops (Utrecht / Lili’s Proto Lab): github.com/LilisProtoLab/osi… • Magnet-specific details: opensourceimaging.org/projec… Hardware is released under CERN-OHL-W. Most software is GPL-3.0. Where AI multiplies the impact Low-field MRI has historically been limited by lower signal-to-noise and greater field inhomogeneity. That is exactly the regime where modern AI thrives. Image reconstruction becomes dramatically better when deep networks trained on high-field data or physics-informed models denoise, correct for inhomogeneity, and push resolution beyond the raw acquisition limits. Real-time sequence adaptation can adjust gradients and RF pulses on the fly as the AI monitors signal quality. Magnet design itself can be optimized by evolutionary algorithms or differentiable physics engines that search for better Halbach geometries or shim placements than human intuition alone can find. Further out, local AI agents turn these scanners into autonomous diagnostic nodes. A small clinic or even a well-equipped garage workshop could run overnight scans, flag anomalies, and queue results for a remote radiologist—or eventually for a specialized medical model. Synthetic data generation from the open designs lets researchers train robust models without proprietary hospital datasets. Robotics integration (patient positioning, coil placement, maintenance) becomes straightforward once the hardware is open and standardized. In the longer arc of the Abundance Interregnum, this is the shape of things: sophisticated medical instruments that no longer require billion-dollar supply chains or national infrastructure. A distributed network of open, AI-augmented low-field scanners could bring advanced imaging to places that have never had it, while simultaneously giving makers, universities, and small labs the ability to experiment, improve, and specialize the technology. The plans are already on the table. The magnets are commercial off-the-shelf. The 3D printers exist in thousands of workshops. The AI tools for reconstruction and design optimization improve every month. What was once the exclusive domain of major hospitals is becoming a community engineering project. This is how abundance arrives—one open, reproducible, AI-extendable system at a time.

No meu discurso de posse em janeiro de 2023 resgatei, porque foi necessário, um compromisso que já havia assumido e honrado nos primeiros dois mandatos: garantir os preceitos constitucionais do direito a uma vida digna, sem fome. Os dados revelados pelo Mapa da Fome da ONU nesta semana reforçam que estamos cumprindo esta missão. Entre 2023 e 2025, o Brasil reduziu em mais de 90% o número de pessoas em insegurança alimentar grave, para 0,6%. O índice chegou a 8,5% nos tempos em que o país retornou ao Mapa da Fome. O resultado é retrato de uma articulação de 80 ações e programas de vários ministérios, com foco no acesso à renda, proteção social e apoio à produção e ao consumo de alimentos adequados, tudo em torno do Plano Brasil sem Fome. Fazem parte dessa equação tanto iniciativas mais conhecidas, como Bolsa Família e Gás do Povo, quanto o Programa de Aquisição de Alimentos, o reajuste e a qualificação da merenda escolar, a volta do financiamento à agricultura familiar, as cozinhas solidárias, o fomento rural, o programa Cisternas, o BPC e o Luz do Povo, para citar alguns. Não à toa, os resultados do Mapa da Fome se conectam com indicadores macroeconômicos que permitem essa melhora da condição de vida de milhões de brasileiros. O PIB acumulou altas nos três últimos anos, a taxa de desemprego registra os menores dados da série histórica, o rendimento médio mensal real domiciliar alcançou o maior valor já registrado pelo IBGE e o salário mínimo voltou a ter ganho real. Como disse naquele discurso de posse, os direitos e interesses da população, o fortalecimento da democracia e a retomada da soberania nacional são pilares de nosso governo.

युवाओं और विद्यार्थियों की भावनाओं को ध्यान में रखते हुए केन्द्रीय शिक्षा मंत्री श्री धर्मेंद्र प्रधान ने अपने पद से इस्तीफ़ा दे दिया है। श्री धर्मेंद्र प्रधान का इस्तीफ़ा इस बात का प्रमाण है कि प्रधानमंत्री श्री नरेंद्र मोदी जी और हमारी सरकार के लिए हमारे विद्यार्थियों और युवाओं की भावनाओं का सम्मान और उनके उज्ज्वल भविष्य के लिये प्रतिबद्धता सर्वोपरि हैं। NEET परीक्षा, पेपर लीक और शिक्षा व्यवस्था में आवश्यक सुधारों को लेकर विद्यार्थियों के मन में जो भी चिंताएँ हैं, उनका पूरी गंभीरता और संवेदनशीलता के साथ समाधान किया जा रहा है। विद्यार्थियों की चिंताओं को गंभीरता से सुनना, उनका समाधान सुनिश्चित करना और उनमें यह विश्वास बनाना कि उनकी आवाज़ सुनी जाएगी और उनकी सभी समस्याओं का समाधान होगा, यही हमारी प्राथमिकता है। मुझे विश्वास है कि अब हमारे युवा और विद्यार्थी पूरे आत्मविश्वास के साथ अपनी पढ़ाई, अपने सपनों और अपनी आकांक्षाओं पर ध्यान केंद्रित करेंगे और एक सशक्त, समृद्ध एवं विकसित भारत के निर्माण में अपना महत्वपूर्ण योगदान देंगे। केंद्रीय मंत्री के रूप में श्री धर्मेंद्र प्रधान जी का कार्यकाल भारत को विकसित राष्ट्र बनाने के संकल्प के प्रति उनके समर्पण का परिचायक रहा है। सार्वजनिक जीवन में उनका योगदान समावेशी, दूरदर्शी और नए भारत की आकांक्षाओं के अनुरूप रहा है।

The advance of two armies and a tank division of the Russian armed forces was repelled: forces of the First Corps Azov of the National Guard of Ukraine destroyed dozens of units of equipment and a large number of occupier personnel. On July 22, the occupiers, using forces of the 8th and 41st Armies along with the 90th Tank Division, attempted an assault in the sector held by the First Corps Azov of the National Guard of Ukraine, involving dozens of units of armored and light vehicles. The 41st Guards Combined Arms Army and the 90th Guards Vitebsk-Novgorod Tank Division of the Russian armed forces advanced from the area of the settlement of Novoekonomichne, while forces of the 8th Guards Combined Arms Army simultaneously advanced from the area of the village of Vozdvyzhenka. For four hours, they attempted to enter settlements in the area of the village of Shakhove. The enemy attempted to deny the sky to Ukrainian forces using "Gerbera" and "Lancet" strike drones. A modern Russian "Tornado-S" MLRS, which was being used to support the assault, was also destroyed. Forces of the First Corps Azov of the National Guard of Ukraine, together with attached units, blocked the path of the advancing mechanized columns. Mine-explosive obstacles were laid on the approaches to the positions of the Ukrainian Defense Forces, and bridges were damaged by tactical aviation. During the assault, the Russians attempted to restore the crossings using pontoons, but these were destroyed by tactical aviation of the Air Force of the Armed Forces of Ukraine (AFU). As a result of the professional actions of all units involved under the command of the First Corps Azov of the National Guard of Ukraine, using barrel artillery, multiple launch rocket systems, and attack drones, the following were destroyed: 7 tanks, 6 armored combat vehicles, 1 BM-21 "Grad" MLRS, 1 "Tornado-S" MLRS, 3 units of special equipment, and 47 units of light vehicles. 123 occupiers were eliminated, and 29 were wounded. The mechanized assault was repelled. We thank the units of the First Corps Azov of the National Guard of Ukraine, the SBU's "A" Special Operations Center, the Unmanned Systems Forces, the Air Force of the AFU, units of the State Border Guard Service of Ukraine, in particular the Main Department of Unmanned Aerial Systems "Fenix," units of the National Guard of Ukraine, and units of the Armed Forces of Ukraine for their professional and courageous actions. Prezydent @NawrockiKn zarzuca, że ustawa wprowadzająca podatek od dodatkowych zysków koncernów paliwowych jest niekonstytucyjna, bo działa wstecz. Najwyraźniej ktoś w Kancelarii @prezydentpl w tej sprawie słabo doradził... Taka ustawa ze swej istoty może dotyczyć tylko sytuacji przeszłej, bo zyski ustala się po upływie określonego czasu. Skoro te nadzwyczajne zyski wystąpiły, wąska grupa przedsiębiorców na tym skorzystała, a skutki są społecznie dotkliwe – częściowo neutralizowane przez działania rządu obniżające podatki od tych paliw – to istnieje konstytucyjne uzasadnienie, aby taki dodatkowy podatek uchwalić. Oczekiwanie, żeby tego typu przepisy działały wyłącznie na przyszłość, to nieporozumienie. Bo trzeba by uchwalić przepisy "na wypadek", gdyby takie dodatkowe zyski (nie wiadomo, w jakiej wysokości) wystąpiły. Nadzwyczajne zyski mogą być opodatkowane wtedy, kiedy już wystąpiły. A konstytucyjność projektu ustawy była weryfikowana przez Rządowe Centrum Legislacji oraz legislatorów Kancelarii Sejmu i Kancelarii Senatu. Raczej nie o ochronę wartości konstytucyjnych chodziło więc Prezydentowi, kiedy pozbawił budżet państwa dochodów od tych dodatkowych zysków koncernów paliwowych. @PremierRP @MF_GOV_PL @Domanski_Andrz

Divisional Commissioner Kashmir, Anshul Garg, said that the recent rains have caused conditions requiring urgent repair and restoration works along the Pahalgam route. To ensure the uninterrupted continuation of the Yatra, comprehensive arrangements have been made on the Baltal axis for the safe and smooth movement of pilgrims. “Due to the recent rains, urgent repair and maintenance works are required to be carried out on the Pahalgam Axis of Shri Amarnathji Yatra. The Yatra shall continue through the Baltal Axis, for which adequate arrangements have been put in place to ensure a smooth and safe pilgrimage,” the Divisional Commissioner said. As of today, more than 3.95 lakh pilgrims have undertaken darshan at the Holy Amarnath Cave Shrine during this year's Yatra, reflecting the successful and peaceful conduct of the pilgrimage."

Russian feedback about using UGVs🔽 1. Before using the UGV, it is necessary to review the route of movement with the UAV for the purpose of passability. UGV can be stuck relatively easily. It is impossible to simply direct the UGV in a certain direction, as is done with tanks or IGVs. This will most likely lead to the loss of the drone. 2. Basically, UGVs are used for restraining actions (distracting attention); in order to maneuver, the group could strike from a second direction. The enemy always hits the UGV, even when they do not pose a real threat to the enemy's strongholds. Machine-gun UGVs cannot defeat soldiers in a trench. UGVs with AGS-17 have limited ammunition and cannot take part in the battle for a long time. The absence of significant targets leads to the fact that the UAV operators still try to defeat the UGV. This allows you to use them to call FPV drone strikes on yourself. 3. If possible, the UGV will drive as close as possible to the point of launch on a cargo vehicle. 4. UGVs break down a lot. Spare batteries and control antennas (retranslators) are needed in large quantities. 5. A UGV is operated by the calculation of 2–3 people. 6. Unlike analog FPV drones, which react almost instantly to control commands, UGVs can react with a delay. Digital channels are used in UGV controls, which often introduce such a delay. 7. UAVs are used to accompany the movement of the UGV. Visibility from the ground is usually insufficient for controlling a UGV. 8. The UGV controlled by radio channels, like the UAVs, requires installation of control antennas and the use of repeaters. 9. It happens that a scheme is being implemented in which the UGV is moving forward on fiber optic and comes back with the help of a management UAV. The duplicating control system, which allows controlling the UGV from the UAV, is also necessary due to the fact that the quality of the cable unwound for the UGV can be low. This, in particular, can lead to the fact that after 200 meters of movement, the image will disappear.

LOOK: The University of the Philippines' Institute for Maritime Affairs and Law of the Sea (IMLOS) has released an updated edition of its West Philippine Sea primer, offering a "concise yet comprehensive" guide to the territorial and maritime disputes from the Philippine perspective. Titled "The West Philippine Sea: The Territorial and Maritime Jurisdiction Disputes from a Filipino Perspective (The WPS Primer 2026)," the 95-page publication builds on the original primer released in 2013 by IMLOS and the UP Asian Center. It incorporates major developments over the past decade, including the landmark 2016 South China Sea Arbitration ruling, which affirmed the Philippines' sovereign rights and jurisdiction over its exclusive economic zone in the West Philippine Sea. The primer is available for free download through the IMLOS website. (📷: UP IMLOS/Facebook)

🔥 Au cœur des feux de forêt, un seul objectif : protéger la population. Engagés en Gironde aux côtés du SDIS 33, les sapeurs-pompiers de Paris poursuivent leur mission dans des conditions particulièrement éprouvantes. Face à un incendie encore difficilement maîtrisable, les équipes sont pleinement mobilisées pour protéger les habitations, contenir la progression des flammes et participer aux évacuations lorsque la situation l'exige. Sur le terrain, les sapeurs-pompiers de Paris, du SDIS 77 et de la Gironde travaillent main dans la main. Au-delà des uniformes et des écussons, c'est une même mission qui les rassemble : préserver des vies, protéger les biens et soutenir les populations confrontées à cette épreuve. Dans ce type d'intervention, chaque geste compte. La coordination, la confiance et la solidarité entre les équipes sont des forces essentielles pour faire face à un feu imprévisible, où les conditions peuvent évoluer en quelques instants. Les journées sont longues, les températures élevées et l'engagement physique est intense. Mais ensemble, les femmes et les hommes engagés sur le terrain avancent avec la même détermination, animés par un seul objectif : remplir leur mission jusqu'au bout. 👏 Courage à l'ensemble des sapeurs-pompiers mobilisés en Gironde. Drowning claims around 300,000 lives every year. That is 30 people every hour. Nearly 1 in 4 are children under 5. As heatwaves become more frequent, more people seek relief in rivers, lakes and the sea, increasing their exposure to drowning risks. Yet drowning is largely preventable. This year’s World Drowning Prevention Day theme, “Unite to turn the tide”, calls for governments, communities and individuals to work together to reduce the toll. Between 2000 and 2021, the global drowning death rate fell by 38%, showing what sustained efforts can achieve. The first-ever Global Strategy for Drowning Prevention aims to build on this progress, targeting 35% fewer deaths by 2035. Governments can accelerate progress by expanding supervised childcare and swimming education, making water sources and pools safer, strengthening flood warnings and safety standards for water transport. Each of us also has a part to play: watch children closely around water, use lifejackets, learn to swim and develop water-safety skills, and never underestimate the risks. These actions can spare thousands of families a devastating loss.

Let's unpack the options for what the US government could do to potentially restrict Chinese AI models: 1. FUD: @deanwball noted the other day that the US government could take a "FUD" approach of just creating lots of doubt and uncertainty about use of Chinese AI, rather than strict legal requirements. (Dean made this point as an analytic matter, he was not advocating for it). The government could issue public security advisories, get sectoral regulators like energy and financial regulators to start raising risks, etc. This might not legally prohibit use, but would likely discourage it. 2. Procurement bans: The U.S. government could use procurement authorities to prohibit the use of Chinese AI models in government contracts, similar to what DoD did to Anthropic earlier this year. This would not prohibit private companies from using Chinese AI models unrelated to government contracts, but it would discourage use and reinforce a FUD approach. 3. Entity List: The Commerce Department could put specific Chinese AI companies (Moonshot, etc.) on the Entity List, which would prohibit exports of US technology to them. Setting aside evasion, this would cut off their access to any remaining US-origin chips not already covered by more general export controls and to US software. It would also potentially complicate U.S. companies’ use of closed or hosted models, as a US company could not send its own software or other "items" to the Chinese company for processing. It would not, however, strictly legally prohibit a U.S. company from downloading an open source model that a Chinese AI company posted online, as the download would not be an export *to* China, but rather an import from it. 4. "ICTS" rule: Commerce's existing "ICTS rule" allows Commerce to restrict the import or US use of a variety of software and other technology that poses a national security risk. Commerce has used the ICTS rule to, inter alia, prevent Americans from using Kaspersky Lab software (from Russia) and it is the basis for the recently-in-the-news restrictions on Polestar autos. Commerce could in theory deploy the rule to prohibit US firms from using Chinese AI models in the US. The one potential caveat to this is that the ICTS Rule exists pursuant to IEEPA, and IEEPA cannot regulate the import (or export) of "information" or "informational materials." I think courts would almost certainly uphold the ICTS rule as applied to the import or use of Chinese-hosted AI models as a prohibition on a “service,” and not on “information.” There would, however, be an interesting question about whether the courts would uphold a ban on a simple US download of an open-source Chinese model, where there was no payment. 5. Sanctions on Chinese AI labs: The President could use IEEPA to impose sanctions on Chinese AI labs, likely after declaring a new national emergency related to adversarial country AI risks. This would block their property in the US and prohibit all US commercial transactions with them. However, IEEPA sanctions would have the same carve out for "information" or "informational materials" as applies to the ICTS rule, and there is some chance the courts would find that IEEPA sanctions cannot prevent a US company from downloading, for free, an open source Chinese model. (Courts, for example, blocked Trump's 2020 use of IEEPA to try to restrict TikTok in the United States). 6. New IEEPA-derived restrictions on US companies using/deploying Chinese AI models: IEEPA is a flexible statute and the Trump Administration could use IEEPA to create new restrictions on the use or deployment of Chinese AI models, for example prohibiting US companies from using the models both in the US and abroad and prohibiting US hyperscalers from making Chinese AI models available in the US or globally. This could either be an outright prohibition, or a restriction, e.g., Chinese models could only be used subject to certain conditions, such as security protocols. (There is some conceptual parallel to how the Department of Justice's Data Security Program works). (There would, however, still be the legal question about whether IEEPA could in fact prevent a US company from simply downloading and using a free Chinese open source model). 7. Congressional legislation: Congress could of course legislate new restrictions on the US use of Chinese AI models. This would avoid the IEEPA limitations discussed above related to “information,” though would still be subject to the First Amendment. I could see the courts upholding a congressional ban on the use of even free open-source AI models despite the first Amendment by finding that such a ban passes “intermediate scrutiny.” (This was part of the basis on which SCOTUS upheld *Congress’s* 2024 legislation requiring a divestment of TikTok after lower courts enjoined Trump’s 2020 IEEPA-based ban). Note: this post is intended solely as a rundown of what the legal options for restrictions are, not a normative argument on what the US government should do.
